summary: Good news if you live in Las Vegas: we checked, and Las Vegas (and Clark County) do not restrict keeping a pet rat. Nevada is broadly permissive about pets (its short list of banned pets is animals like foxes and skunks, not rats), and the local exotic-animal permit (Clark County ch. 10.18; Las Vegas Title 7) targets genuinely exotic or dangerous animals. The county treats wild, non-domestic rats as a pest-control matter, separate from a domesticated pet rat. A pet roof rat is allowed.

keep.why: Nevada does not restrict keeping a domesticated pet rat; the state's commonly-cited illegal pets are species such as foxes and skunks, not rats. Clark County ch. 10.18 (Exotic or Wild Animals) and Las Vegas Title 7 require permits for genuinely exotic or dangerous animals, which a domesticated pet rat is not; the county directs wild, non-domestic rat issues to pest control, distinguishing them from pet rats. Not stricter than Nevada. Medium confidence: the exact Clark County exotic-animal definition is on a code host that blocked a direct read, so this rests on Nevada's permissive pet framework plus the county's wild-versus-pet rat distinction.
keep.governing_law: Clark County Code ch. 10.18 (Exotic or Wild Animals); Las Vegas Municipal Code Title 7 (Animals); Nevada pet law generally.

breed.why: No local rodent-breeding restriction; the state's permissive rule applies.

sell_give.why: No local restriction on giving or selling a pet rat; the state's rule applies.

transport.why: No local transport restriction on a pet rat; the state's rule applies.
